answer: A citizen-science site could renew accounts monthly by having them trace a vine in each assigned photo, marking shoots that spiral around supports or wander across the ground. Disjoint assignments and a one-credit-per-photo ledger prevent reuse; a random 20% expert audit rejects batches with bad traces. More identities require more distinct annotation work. Example: requiring 40 accepted photo traces per identity per month makes 25 fake identities cost 1,000 distinct accepted traces, with none credited twice.
